diagnosis_explanation: Your baby was born early. This means your baby was not fully developed. Your baby had some trouble breathing. This is called respiratory distress. Doctors also checked to see if your baby had an infection. This is called sepsis. Your baby is now stable.
medication_rationale:
Ampicillin - stopping:
Your doctor wants you to stop taking this medicine. Your baby's blood cultures were negative. Do not take it until your doctor tells you it is safe to start again.

Gentamicin - stopping:
Your doctor wants you to stop taking this medicine. Your baby's blood cultures were negative. Do not take it until your doctor tells you it is safe to start again.

EBM 22 22 per os:
This special formula is for your baby. It helps your baby grow and gain weight. You will give this by mouth.

NeoSure per os:
This special formula is for your baby. It helps your baby grow and gain weight. It is added to breast milk. You will give this by mouth.

EBM 22 22 ad lib:
This special formula is for your baby. It helps your baby grow and gain weight. Your baby will eat this when hungry.

NeoSure ad lib:
This special formula is for your baby. It helps your baby grow and gain weight. Your baby will eat this when hungry. It is added to breast milk.
recovery_trajectory:
**Week 1:**
- You will feel tired and may have less energy. This is normal.
- Feed your baby NeoSure and breast milk or formula as scheduled.
- Your baby should eat 2 to 3 ounces per feeding.
- Feed your baby when they seem hungry. This is called ad lib feeding.
- Watch for signs that your baby needs to see the doctor.
- Your baby's goal is to eat well and rest this week.
- Call your doctor if your baby has trouble breathing.
- Call your doctor if your baby refuses to eat.

**Week 2:**
- Your baby may start to feel a little stronger.
- Continue feeding your baby as before.
- Stick to the 2 to 3 ounces per feed.
- Feed your baby on demand.
- Your baby's goal is to gain weight steadily.
- Watch for normal feeding and sleeping patterns.
- Call your doctor if your baby seems weak or very sleepy.

**Week 3:**
- Your baby might become more alert and interactive.
- Keep following the feeding schedule with NeoSure.
- Continue ad lib feeding on demand.
- Your baby's goal is to improve feeding endurance.
- Look for signs of normal stooling and wet diapers.
- Call your doctor if your baby has a fever over 100.4 F.
- Call your doctor if your baby seems uncomfortable when eating.

**Week 4:**
- Your baby should show more consistent gains in strength.
- Continue the current feeding plan.
- Feed your baby on demand as needed.
- Your baby's goal is to establish a routine.
- Watch for your baby's social cues and interactions.
- Call your doctor if your baby has persistent vomiting.

**When to expect improvement:**
- Your baby's strength and feeding should get better each week.
- Keep up with the feeding schedule and plan.
- Continue to watch your baby for any new concerns.
- Follow your doctor's advice for ongoing care.
